life: Hardy herbaceous perennial, 2–4 ft, spreading by rhizomes
other_uses: Among the strongest pollinator plants of any North American native — mountain mints are consistently top-ranked in pollinator trials, drawing bees, wasps, flies and butterflies over a long bloom.
prep: Leaves used fresh or dried as a mint-like seasoning and tea; the flavour is strong and slightly camphorous, so use sparingly.
harvest: Leaves before and during bloom, July–September.
risks: Strongly aromatic; large medicinal doses are not advised in pregnancy, as with other mints. Spreads by rhizome — give it room or contain it.
buy: Native nurseries and regional seed suppliers.
